name: Bainouk-Samik
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Quint, Nicolas. 2024. Djifanghor Nyun (Baïnounk). In Lüpke (ed.), The Oxford Guide to the Atlantic Languages of West Africa, 291-317 (HAL author copy)
sources.note: Sister language (Gufangor, gube1234), not this variety: sec. 13.3.1.3 p. 296 'JFG is a stress language'; stress on the lexical root, first root syllable or heaviest syllable; demarcative only. Recorded here only as the nearest-relative statement.

sources.citation: Cobbinah, Alexander Yao. 2013. Nominal classification and verbal nouns in Baïnounk Gubëeher. PhD thesis, SOAS. 483 pp. (CORE mirror)
sources.note: Sister language (Gubëeher, gube1234). Sec. 2.2 Phonology covers consonants, vowels, harmony, assimilation; no token 'stress'/'accent'/'tone' in a linguistic sense. Gujaher mentioned only as the variety of the Samik/Jegui area documented by Lüpke (pp. 31-34 identity discussion).

sources.citation: Cobbinah, Alexander & Laurent Manga. 2014. Dictionnaire (préliminaire) Baïnounk Gubëeher – Français. Djibonker, ms. (Crossroads project upload, Wayback copy)
sources.note: Sister language. Orthography section (PDF pp. 5-9) describes vowel length and ATR harmony ('accent aigu' marks vowel quality, not stress); phonetic transcriptions carry no stress marks; nothing on stress, accent or tone.

sources.citation: Lüpke, Friederike. 2014-2017. Sixteen talk handouts / drafts from the SOAS Crossroads project site (Sédhiou 2016, PLM 2016, Chicago 2017, Reading 2017, Greifswald, The Hague, Rio, Michicagoan, Düsseldorf x2, Leipzig, Cologne, 'Escaping the tyranny of writing', LILIEMA policy brief; Cobbinah publication list)
sources.note: Nothing: all sociolinguistic or noun-class morphology; zero linguistic 'stress'/'accent'/'tone' tokens across all files.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record bain1260 'Bainouk-Samik' (bookkeeping=true), with Ethnologue comment: 'this split cannot be motivated by anything except the Senegal-Guinea Bissau national border (Lüpke 2010:159, Cobbinah 2013:31-34)... See also: Bainounk-Gujaher [bab]'
sources.note: Nothing; identity record only. Only MEDs are Moseley 2010 and Ethnologue 2009 (wordlist_or_less).

sources.citation: Lüpke, Friederike. 2010. Language and identity in flux: in search of Baïnounk. Journal of Language Contact THEMA 3: 155-174 (whole-issue PDF)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p. 159: 'A third Baïnounk language listed by the Ethnologue is Baïnounk-Samik (1685 speakers), which probably corresponds to Baïnounk Gujaher, since this variety is spoken in and around the village of Samik.' Sociolinguistic paper.
